title: A Novel Modulator of Resistance for Oxaliplatin-Based Therapy for Colorectal Cancer: The Escrt Family Member VPS4A
content: Drug resistance is still one of the main challenges for the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). Whilst some resistance mechanisms are well-known, from the static therapy success rate clearly still much is undiscovered. Intracellular transport mechanisms have come under attention as having a possible role in drug resistance, and here the Endosomal Sorting Complex Required for Transport (ESCRT) protein family is studied as a source of drug resistance modulation using human CRC cell lines and clinical material. From initial screening of ESCRT proteins in a panel of 10 CRC wild-type cell lines using immunoblotting, Vacuolar Protein Sorting-Associated Protein A4 (VPS4A) was identified as being consistently highly expressed, and this was selected for further investigation. Immunohistopathological evaluation in a small panel of CRC patient samples demonstrated high expression in the tumour epithelium compared to normal intestinal epithelium. Knockdown of VPS4A resulted in enhanced sensitivity of cells to oxaliplatin, and not the other two commonly used drugs, 5-fluorouracil and irinotecan, and it was subsequently seen that oxaliplatin-resistant sublines had significantly higher VPS4A expression than their wild-type variants. In addition, it was demonstrated that a small molecule inhibitor of VPS4A, aloperine, could interact synergistically with oxaliplatin to enhance its sensitivity in an oxaliplatin-resistant cell line. The evidence presented here thus indicates that ESCRT machinery, specifically VPS4A, may act as a modulator of oxaliplatin resistance in CRC.
